verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed against both rendered pages at 300 dpi. PDF page 399 (printed folio 369, E:/Temp/specrecon/v400_399/spec_p399.png): after the Format 2 (elementary) general format diagram, the final body line of the page is a standalone paragraph reading exactly 'where entry-name-clause is described in 13.18.20, Entry-name clause' with NO terminating period, followed only by the footer 'ISO/IEC 2023 369'. PDF page 400 (printed folio 370, E:/Temp/specrecon/v400/spec_p400.png): below the running header 'ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)', the first body element is its own separate paragraph 'where screen-attribute-clauses is:', with the bracketed BELL / BLINK / HIGHLIGHT-LOWLIGHT / REVERSE-VIDEO / UNDERLINE / FOREGROUND-COLOR / BACKGROUND-COLOR stack beneath it. These are unambiguously two distinct paragraphs on two distinct pages. The markdown at line 17157 concatenates them into a single line with only a space between 'Entry-name clause' and 'where screen-attribute-clauses is:' (verified byte-exact: line 17156 blank, 17157 the fused text, 17158 blank, 17159 the anchor, 17160 '## Page 400', 17161 the running header, 17162-17163 blank, 17164 the opening fence). Refutation attempts all fail: (1) no text is missing, but this is not a 'missing text' claim - it is a lost paragraph boundary; (2) it is not line wrapping or hyphenation, because the transcription's own convention elsewhere is a standalone introducer line directly above the fence (line 17185 'where picture-clause is described in 13.18.40, PICTURE clause.' and line 17187 'where source-destination-clauses is:' are each on their own line), so line 17157 is a deviation from the file's own established pattern; (3) it is not merely page-break furniture, because the fusion changes meaning - the run-on reads as though `screen-attribute-clauses` were being defined inside 13.18.20 Entry-name clause, a false cross-reference binding that the spec does not make; (4) the claim does not misquote either source - both quotations are verbatim, and the absence of a period after 'Entry-name clause' is correct in the PDF too (the identical sentence at markdown line 21210, under 13.18.44.2 REDEFINES, is likewise period-less and correctly standalone, confirming the transcription convention and isolating line 17157 as the defect). The claim is accurate on every checkable point.
verdict.corrected_description: Real, and described accurately, with two refinements of nuance. (a) The defect is a lost PARAGRAPH BOUNDARY, not lost text: every word of both sentences is present. Two distinct spec paragraphs - the last body line of page 399, 'where entry-name-clause is described in 13.18.20, Entry-name clause', and the first body line of page 400, 'where screen-attribute-clauses is:' - are fused into a single markdown line (17157) separated only by a space. The correct repair is to split line 17157 into two paragraphs and move the second one to AFTER the anchor and the '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' running header, immediately above the opening ``` fence at line 17164, matching the file's own convention at lines 17185 and 17187. Note that neither sentence takes a terminating period in the printed standard, so no period should be introduced when splitting. (b) The figure is not left entirely unnamed in the transcription: the editorial block immediately below the fence begins '> **Figure notes (screen-attribute-clauses syntax diagram).**', so a reader of the page-400 slice can still recover the name. That is a transcriber's annotation rather than spec text, however, so the spec's OWN introducer sentence is still misattributed to page 399 and the structural severity rating stands.
